definition: firmness of character; unyielding courage; passion and perseverance for long-term goals
koreanMeaning: 끈기, 투지; 장기 목표를 향한 열정과 인내
etymology: Old English 'grēot' (sand, gravel) → Middle English 'grit' (coarse particles) → metaphor for toughness and endurance
contextSentence: It was grit. Grit is passion and perseverance for very long-term goals.
contextSentenceKo: 그것은 끈기였습니다. 끈기란 매우 장기적인 목표를 향한 열정과 인내입니다.

definition: persistence in doing something despite difficulty or delay in achieving success
contextSentence: Grit is passion and perseverance for very long-term goals.
contextSentenceKo: 끈기란 매우 장기적인 목표를 향한 열정과 인내입니다.

definition: the ability to sustain prolonged physical or mental effort
koreanMeaning: 체력, 지구력; 장시간 노력을 지속하는 능력
etymology: Latin 'stamina' (threads of life spun by the Fates) ← plural of 'stamen' (thread, fiber)

definition: extremely high; reaching the stratosphere (figuratively: exceptionally great)
etymology: Latin 'stratum' (layer) + Greek 'sphaira' (sphere) + '-ic' → relating to the upper atmosphere → metaphor for extremely high
contextSentence: Some of my strongest performers did not have stratospheric IQ scores.
contextSentenceKo: 가장 뛰어난 성과를 낸 학생들 중 일부는 엄청나게 높은 IQ 점수를 가지고 있지 않았습니다.

definition: a four-sided shape with opposite sides parallel and equal in length
contextSentence: Ratios, decimals, the area of a parallelogram.

definition: a thing that predicts; a factor indicating a future outcome
contextSentence: One characteristic emerged as a significant predictor of success.
contextSentenceKo: 하나의 특성이 성공의 유의미한 예측 인자로 나타났습니다.

definition: a young trainee in the armed services or police force
contextSentence: We tried to predict which cadets would stay in military training and which would drop out.
contextSentenceKo: 어떤 사관생도가 군사 훈련에 남고 어떤 생도가 중퇴할지 예측하려고 했습니다.

definition: in an opposite manner; in reverse proportion
contextSentence: Grit is usually unrelated or even inversely related to measures of talent.
contextSentenceKo: 끈기는 보통 재능의 척도와 무관하거나 심지어 반비례하는 관계입니다.

definition: a set of printed questions used for gathering information from respondents
contextSentence: I asked thousands of high school juniors to take grit questionnaires.
contextSentenceKo: 수천 명의 고등학교 3학년 학생들에게 끈기 설문지를 작성하도록 했습니다.

definition: the ability to understand something immediately, without conscious reasoning
etymology: Latin 'intuitio' (a looking at) ← 'intueri' (to look at, consider) ← 'in-' (at) + 'tueri' (to look)
contextSentence: We need to take our best ideas, our strongest intuitions, and we need to test them.
contextSentenceKo: 우리의 최고의 아이디어와 가장 강한 직관을 가지고 검증해야 합니다.

definition: the business of giving expert advice to people working in a professional field
etymology: Latin 'consultare' (to deliberate, take counsel) ← 'consulere' (to take counsel)
contextSentence: I left a very demanding job in management consulting.
contextSentenceKo: 매우 힘든 경영 컨설팅 직장을 떠났습니다.

definition: a person new to a job, activity, or organization; a beginner
etymology: possibly alteration of 'recruit'; origin uncertain, first recorded in American English 1890s
contextSentence: We studied rookie teachers working in really tough neighborhoods.
contextSentenceKo: 정말 어려운 지역에서 일하는 신입 교사들을 연구했습니다.

definition: a pledge or obligation; dedication to a cause or activity
contextSentence: There are many talented individuals who simply do not follow through on their commitments.
contextSentenceKo: 자신의 약속을 끝까지 이행하지 않는 재능 있는 사람들이 많습니다.

definition: the established set of attitudes held by someone; a way of thinking
etymology: 'mind' (Old English 'gemynd', memory) + 'set' (Old English 'settan', to place) — compound coined 1930s
contextSentence: The best idea I've heard about building grit in kids is something called growth mindset.
contextSentenceKo: 아이들의 끈기를 키우는 것에 대해 제가 들은 최고의 아이디어는 성장 마인드셋이라는 것입니다.

definition: in a way that is large or important enough to have an effect or be noticed
contextSentence: Grittier kids were significantly more likely to graduate.
contextSentenceKo: 끈기가 더 강한 아이들이 졸업할 가능성이 상당히 더 높았습니다.
